Appearance

Write lean Lua dynamic backends powered by Rust

Nitr serves HTTP with embedded Lua 5.4. You write the dynamic logic parts. The routing, SQLite, templates, crypto and the rest of HTTP are already Rust and every script runs inside a sandbox.

Get started GitHub
  • One binary
  • Lua 5.4, sandboxed
  • MIT / Apache-2.0

Why Nitr

A scripting language where it helps, Rust where it matters

Dynamic handlers should be quick to write and easy to change. Nitr combines the simplicity of Lua with the performance, safety, and reliability of Rust; so the infrastructure stays out of your way.

Parallel by construction

A fixed pool of independent Lua states, one per CPU core. No global lock, because there is no global interpreter.

Safe by default

No io or os, an 8 MiB heap cap, and an execution budget that actually stops while true do end.

One-file deploys

nitr build packs config, Lua, templates, static files and migrations into a single executable.

One namespace

Everything lives under nitr.*, and your own Rust modules mount at nitr.ext.*, where no builtin can collide.

Batteries included

The tedious parts of HTTP are already written

And they run in Rust, before a Lua state is even checked out.

Rust-side routing

Path parameters, middleware composed at load, 404/405 answered without entering Lua.

SQLite that behaves

WAL, busy timeout and foreign keys on; plain-SQL migrations, checksummed.

Templates

minijinja rendering, with escaping on by default.

Outbound HTTP

Shared pool, timeouts, opt-in retries, and an SSRF policy DNS rebinding cannot slip past.

Static files

ETag, 304, range requests, traversal protection, precompressed sidecars.

Compression & CORS

brotli/gzip on demand; preflights answered before Lua runs.

Uploads out of the heap

Multipart parts stream straight to disk, in Rust.

Streaming & SSE

Writer callbacks and coroutine bodies, with real backpressure.

Crypto & auth

argon2id, HMAC, AEAD, JWTs that cannot accept alg: none.

Sessions & CSRF

Signed cookies, stateless sessions, double-submit CSRF middleware.

Validation

Schemas compiled once, checked in Rust, undeclared fields stripped.

Structured logs

JSON with real keys, request spans, and strict redaction rules.

A test framework

describe/it/expect, dispatching through the real router.

Hot reload

nitr dev rebuilds on save; SIGHUP reloads without dropping connections.

Health & graceful drain

Rust-owned /healthz and /readyz; readiness flips before a drain can fail a request.

Editor completion

Generated LuaCATS types for the whole nitr.* surface.

Configuration

One file, validated before it runs.

Describe the server in readable TOML, override any of it with NITR_* variables or flags, and let unknown keys fail loudly instead of silently.

  • Flags > environment > file > defaults, in that order.
  • Typos, contradictions and missing paths refuse to start.
  • nitr check --print-config shows which value won.
See all options →

Extensible

Bring your own Rust modules.

Nitr is also a library crate. Mount your own Rust modules into every Lua state at nitr.ext.* — one level below the standard library, so no future builtin can ever collide with them.

  • Rust owns what happens inside: shared state, I/O, native speed.
  • Lua only composes it, still under its memory and time budget.
  • Third-party extension crates need no fork.
How extension modules work →

Get started

An application in three commands

Nitr is in early development and not ready for production. Install it from source with a Rust toolchain. 

cargo install --git https://github.com/joseluisq/nitr nitr-cli

Then scaffold, migrate and run:

nitr init && nitr migrate && nitr dev
